title: Mission, philosophy, and family partnership
excerpt: St. Martha describes its mission as forming students through prayer, study, and service in a loving, Christ-like environment. The section also explains the school's Catholic philosophy and expectations for family partnership.

title: School hours and enrollment
excerpt: Before-school care begins at 7:20 a.m.; the school day runs from 8:00 a.m. to 3:25 p.m.; after-school care runs until 6:00 p.m. This section also explains the annual enrollment order and waiting-list process.

title: Tuition, assistance, payments, and withdrawal
excerpt: Tuition and fees are set annually. The handbook outlines assistance applications, FACTS payment expectations, RaiseRight credits, nonrefundable fees, and the withdrawal refund schedule.

title: Attendance, absences, and tardiness
excerpt: Families should report absences to the school office. Students may enter at 7:50 a.m. and are marked tardy if they are not in class by 8:00 a.m.; arriving after 10:00 a.m. or leaving before 1:00 p.m. counts as a half-day absence.

title: Conferences, homework, make-up work, and report cards
excerpt: The academic policies cover parent-teacher conferences, homework expectations, work missed during absences, quarterly K–8 report cards in SchoolSpeak, and NWEA testing for grades 3–8.

title: Field trips and chaperones
excerpt: Field trips are treated as the curriculum for the day. The policy covers permission forms, transportation and driver documentation, student behavior, chaperones, and younger siblings.

title: Arrival, dismissal, carline, and pickup
excerpt: This section gives separate morning and dismissal procedures for preschool and kindergarten and for grades 1–8, including carline directions, late arrivals, authorized pickup, and driveway safety.

title: Birthdays, recess, sports, parking, and school security
excerpt: Policies cover classroom birthday treats and invitations, birthday free dress, outdoor recess weather guidance, extracurricular sports, parking-lot conduct, locked-door procedures, and visitor check-in.

title: Volunteer requirements
excerpt: Each family is asked to contribute at least 20 volunteer hours per school year. Volunteers working with students must meet diocesan child-protection and background-check requirements and register in the school office.

title: Uniforms, dress code, free dress, and spirit wear
excerpt: The handbook explains required uniform sources, general appearance rules, free-dress and spirit-wear expectations, accessories, shoes, seasonal options, and grade-specific K–8 uniform guidelines.

title: Health, allergies, illness, immunizations, and medication
excerpt: Families must notify the school about allergies and health needs. The section covers allergy action plans and EpiPens, illness and communicable disease, immunization records, and the forms and original containers required for medication at school.

title: Student mental health and safety
excerpt: The handbook asks families and staff to report concerning behavior, describes the school's support approach, and lists local and regional mental-health resources for families.

title: Safety, emergencies, weather, drills, and school closings
excerpt: The safety section covers fire and tornado drills, lockdowns, school-closing notices, hazardous travel, the school crisis plan, asbestos notices, child-protection reporting, and the weapons policy.

title: School communication and addressing concerns
excerpt: The handbook identifies SchoolSpeak and Tuesday News Notes as primary communication channels, sets a weekday email-response expectation, and gives a step-by-step path for raising academic or behavior concerns.

title: Weekly liturgy and lunch program
excerpt: School Mass is held Thursdays at 8:20 a.m., with additional grade-level Masses noted in the handbook. The lunch section explains the Lansing Catholic catered program, FACTS balances, ordering, packed lunches, and classroom food rules.

title: Discipline, virtues, and general school rules
excerpt: Discipline is presented as moral guidance grounded in Gospel values. These pages outline Education in Virtue, student responsibilities, personal-device rules, academic honesty, classroom expectations, playground rules, restorative practices, and possible consequences.

title: Physical conduct, discriminatory language, bullying, and harassment
excerpt: The conduct policies define and address severe physical aggression, rough play, discriminatory or offensive language, bullying versus conflict, threats, cyberbullying, and sexual harassment, with grade-level consequence tables.

title: Kids' Corner before- and after-school care
excerpt: The childcare section covers program objectives, 7:20–7:50 a.m. and 3:25–6:00 p.m. hours, registration documents, sign-in and pickup, late pickup, before-care procedures, fees, and billing.

title: Technology policy and copyright
excerpt: The handbook points families to a separate cellphone, Chromebook, and technology acceptable-use policy and summarizes U.S. copyright protections and fair-use considerations.

title: Handbook acknowledgment and signature page
excerpt: The final content page contains the diocesan requirement, parent initials and signature lines, student signatures for grades 4–8, and a list of handbook updates for 2025–26.
